title: Dispatch: Sol confirmation repairs batch C (attempt 1)
description:
Repair batch C for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8: the Sol confirmation review (bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.4 — run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.4` and read S3, S4, S5, S8, S11, S14, S16, S17, S18 in full; each has fresh reproduced failures) found these still open or new. Earlier repair context: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1`, `.8.2`, `.8.3`. This is the second repair cycle for S3/S4/S5: fix the CLASS, not the example — every failure family listed under each finding must be closed and tested. You own all files needed. No new migration unless strictly unavoidable (if unavoidable, 0037, and record why).

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
S3 (terminal death, both death-rule modes): (a) a combatant whose status is 'dead' stays dead: any explicit status other than 'dead' is refused, and any positive hpDelta is refused — in BOTH monster and player-character modes when the death came from exhaustion level 6 or zero heads; in player-character mode for any death; monster-mode ordinary revival-by-healing (pre-existing behaviour) stays only when neither exhaustion 6 nor zero heads applies. 'inactive' is no longer accepted for a dead combatant (a dead combatant needs no removal). (b) Under player-character rules, an explicit 'escaped' or 'inactive' status in the SAME call as an hpDelta is refused ("apply damage and participation status in separate calls"), so participation status never suppresses lifecycle derivation. (c) Exhaustion level 6 is terminal in both modes on every write.
S4 (actor lifecycle continuity): every write that changes head_count, heads_died_since_own_turn, fire_damage_since_own_turn, death_rules, counters, recovery block, or recovery schedule syncs the campaign actor's combatLifecycle in the same transaction — including head settlement with suppressed or zero healing (sync must not depend on a healing call). combatLifecycle also persists and transfers the pending own-turn facts (headsDiedSinceOwnTurn, fireDamageSinceOwnTurn) so a close/reopen before the creature's next own-turn end keeps the pending regrowth/suppression. Per-turn damage accumulation (damage_this_turn, damage_turn_key, head_died_this_turn) is turn-scoped and does not transfer.
S5 (projection ownership): the actor's current projection is: the row in the ACTIVE combat instance if one exists for that identity; otherwise the row whose combat_instance was inserted last (SQLite rowid of combat_instance — insertion order), never timestamps or lexical ids. One shared helper decides it, used by actor sync, recovery-schedule transfer, and resolveCombatantRecoveries. Test equal timestamps with ascending, descending, and custom ids.
S8 (HP admission): start_encounter / any projection of an actor or creature into a combatant row clamps hp_current to effectiveHpMax(hp_max, conditions) through the non-damage clamp of S18 (never damage), for supplied, defaulted, and inherited HP; the actor row is written consistently. A clamp to 0 applies the 0-HP lifecycle for the death mode.
S11 (unknown head state): keep the explicit refusal for a multi-head combatant with NULL head_count, but make the message truthful: the head count is unknown because this creature's state predates head tracking, Eshyra cannot reconstruct it, and head-dependent operations (damage, healing, turn settlement, extra reactions) are refused for it. Do not promise that restarting the encounter fixes it, and do not reset heads to the source value. Test the recurring-actor retry path asserts the truthful continued refusal.
S14 (zero effective maximum): regaining hit points is capped at the effective maximum for characters and combatants on every path (heal, natural-20 death save, clock stable recovery, regrowth healing). When the cap leaves 0 HP regained: a natural 20 counts as one death-save success (like the suffocation block) and never reports 'revived'; healing at a zero maximum changes nothing (no alive, no counter reset; report 0 regained); a due stable recovery at a zero maximum regains nothing and clears its deadline while the creature stays stable. Revival and counter resets happen only when HP actually rises above 0. Do not restore any minimum-one rule.
S16 (ammunition reuse): the guard in ammunition.ts refuses a new expenditure only when the physical row is referenced by an UNRESOLVED ('expended') expenditure; resolved history never blocks re-firing recovered ammunition. Keep the no-double-unresolved-accounting proof; add a two-battle recover-then-re-expend test over whole, partial, and single-piece rows.
S17 (reserved lifecycle state): the combatLifecycle key in campaign_actor.state_json is engine-owned. start_encounter actors[].state (and every other model-facing input that writes actor state) refuses a combatLifecycle key with a clear error, and updating an actor's other state preserves the existing combatLifecycle subtree untouched (merge, never replace). New lifecycle facts are initialized only from source/engine transitions.
S18 (non-damage clamp): add explicit non-damage clamp operations — characters in hpLifecycle.ts, combatants in encounterCombatants.ts — that lower hp_current to the effective maximum without touching temporary HP, damage-per-turn accounting, head loss, death-save failures, or concentration DCs; if the clamp brings HP from above 0 to 0, apply the 0-HP lifecycle (character → dying with concentration break as incapacitation; monster combatant → dead; player-character combatant → dying) atomically, with actor sync. adjust_exhaustion uses these instead of adjustHp/updateCombatant hpDelta, and returns the persisted HP.

TESTS (generalized matrices, through the registry where model-facing): S3 transition matrix over mode × alive/dying/stable/dead × explicit statuses × lethal damage × multi-step dead→(any status)→heal; S4 close/reopen before and after settlement × recovery block × fire, asserting actor lifecycle equals the combatant row; S5 equal-timestamp ordering cases for sync and recovery; S8 admission over supplied/defaulted/inherited HP × exhaustion below/above 4 × odd/even maxima × zero-result lifecycle; S11 retry refusal text; S14 characters/combatants × effective max 0/1/greater × nat-20/heal/stable-deadline/regrowth; S16 two-battle reuse; S17 injection/removal/replacement refused and unrelated state preserved; S18 temp HP absent/below/above the clamp, hydra head and damage counters unchanged, zero-result lifecycle. Map each finding to its tests in your notes.
acceptance_criteria: All listed findings repaired with the listed tests; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report mapping findings to tests in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
notes:
Dispatched gpt-6-luna high, pgid 2823898, off eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8@e601316c.
Implemented and committed as 44db0884 on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.5. Files changed: packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts, actionEconomy.ts, ammunition.ts, exhaustionMutation.ts, hpLifecycle.ts; tests in activeEffects.test.ts, ammunition.test.ts, encounterCombatants.test.ts, exhaustion.test.ts. No migration was needed. No design deviations were forced by the code. The activeEffects concentration test now expects refusal when a dead combatant is assigned another status, matching the accepted terminal-death rule.

Finding-to-test mapping:
S3 — encounterCombatants.test.ts: derives lethal lifecycle before participation status and keeps monster exhaustion-six terminal; keeps dead player-character combatants terminal and rejects removal status; keeps exhaustion-six player-character combatants dead on every update; existing dying/stable damage and death-save lifecycle cases. activeEffects.test.ts asserts concentration break occurs on lethal transition and dead status cannot be rewritten.
S4 — encounterCombatants.test.ts: transfers pending hydra regrowth facts and syncs settlement without healing; carries a recurring actor combat lifecycle through encounter projections. The first covers close/reopen before settlement with healing blocked; actor lifecycle is checked against the combatant row after settlement.
S5 — encounterCombatants.test.ts: insertion-order projection test matrix for ascending, descending, and custom ids at equal timestamps; carries a recurring actor combat lifecycle through encounter projections exercises transferred stable recovery and clock resolution. Sync, transfer, and recovery use isCurrentActorProjection.
S8 — exhaustion.test.ts: clamps encounter actor HP at admission and enters the zero-HP lifecycle; encounterCombatants.test.ts: clamps model supplied actor HP to the condition-adjusted maximum on admission; existing effectiveHpMax floor tests cover odd/even and zero-result lifecycle clamps.
S11 — encounterCombatants.test.ts: reports truthful continued refusal for an unknown recurring hydra head count after a harmless update, close, and retry.
S14 — exhaustion.test.ts: does not revive at zero effective maximum on a natural 20; clears due stable recovery at zero maximum without reviving either target; existing player-combatant healing cap test. The recovery tests assert deadline clearing and persistent dying/stable state.
S16 — ammunition.test.ts: recovered physical rows can be expended in a later battle for whole, partial, and one-piece recovered rows; existing tracks each physical split row once and never returns more than half expended preserves the unresolved-accounting proof.
S17 — exhaustion.test.ts: rejects model injection of actor combat lifecycle at encounter admission; encounterCombatants.test.ts: preserves actor lifecycle when unrelated state metadata is updated, plus lifecycle continuity assertions through recurring projections.
S18 — exhaustion.test.ts: uses non-damage clamps without consuming temp HP or inventing hydra damage; existing zero-HP clamp lifecycle cases verify character dying and combatant mode behavior.

Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed after the final source and test edits: format/check passed, forced typecheck passed, and 320 test files passed with 2 documented skipped; 5,688 tests passed and 3 documented skipped. git diff --check passed. No follow-up beads were found.
